newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-STARS TOP DEVILS TO IMPROVE TO LEAGUE-BEST 4-0.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-STARS TOP DEVILS TO IMPROVE TO LEAGUE-BEST 4-0.

text.p: Darryl Sydor, Pat Verbeek and Brent Gilchrist scored third-period goals as the Dallas Stars improved to a league-best 4-0 with a 4-2 victory over the New Jersey Devils on Saturday.
The Stars, off to their best start in franchise history, are the only unbeaten, untied team left in the National Hockey League.
Sydor tied the game 2-2 by lifting a shot over Devils' goaltender Martin Brodeur's left shoulder with 17:28 left.

Verbeek, who has a point in all four games, broke the deadlock at 7:11 when he finished a 2-on-1 with Benoit Hogue, beating Brodeur low to the stick side. Gilchrist added an empty netter with 38 seconds left to seal the victory.
Bobby Holik had a goal and an assist for the Devils, but Arturs Irbe made 27 saves in goal for Dallas.

"Both New Jersey and the Rangers were a good test for us," said Stars coach Ken Hitchcock. "We're off to a 4-0 start, but you can't fall in love with yourself. We're going to take it one game at a time."
At Florida, John Vanbiesbrouck stopped 21 shots for his 24th career shoutout and the Panthers scored twice in each period for a 6-0 rout of previously unbeaten Hartford.
Six different players scored for Florida, spoiling the Whalers debut of Paul Coffey and Keith Primeau, who were acquired from Detroit earlier in the week.
Ray Sheppard and Tom Fitzgerald beat Hartford goalie Sean Burke 37 seconds apart midway through the first period. Stu Barnes assisted on three goals for Florida, which outshot Hartford 32-21.
In Montreal, Valeri Bure scored twice and Pierre Turgeon had three assists to lead the unbeaten Canadiens to a 5-2 victory over the winless New York Rangers.

Brian Savage scored the lone goal of the first period on a Montreal powerplay at 9:38. The Canadiens then erupted for three goals in the first 5:16 of the second and never looked back. Benoit Brunet, Bure and Vincent Damphousse chased Mike Richter from the New York net.
Bure's second goal of the four-goal second period made it 5-0 as Montreal improved to 2-0-2.
In Pittsburgh, Mario Lemieux's unassisted goal with just under eight minutes to go lifted the Penguins to their first win of the season, a 3-2 victory over the Ottawa Senators.
Lemieux skated around the Ottawa net and banked the puck off rookie defenceman Wade Redden's skate past a surprised Ron Tugnutt for his fourth goal of the season.
Ken Wregget made 28 saves for Pittsburgh, while Tugnutt stopped 32 shots.
Alexei Yashin had a goal and an assist for the Senators, who beat Pittsburgh on Friday.

On Long Island, Marty McInnis and Derek King each scored twice and Eric Fichaud came within 31 seconds of a shutout as the New York Islanders posted their first win, a 5-1 triumph over the Philadelphia Flyers.

Fichaud made 29 saves, but lost his shutout bid when Trent Klatt scored a controversial goal at 19:29 of the third. Klatt appeared to be in the crease when he jammed home Craig Darby's centering pass.
In Buffalo, Steve Yzerman and Igor Larionov each had a goal and two assists as the Detroit Red Wings spoiled the Sabres' first regular-season game at the new Marine Midland Arena with a 6-1 rout.
Slava Kozlov scored in the first period and Yzerman tallied on a breakaway in the second. Detroit blew the game open in the third with three goals in a 2:15 span.
Mike Peca was the only player to beat Detroit's Mike Vernon when he scored at 5:24 of the third.

In Toronto, Chris Gratton scored twice in a four-goal first period and completed his first career hat trick in the final second with an empty netter as the Tampa Bay Lightning beat the Maple Leafs 7-4.
Corey Schwab, starting in place of the injured Darren Puppa, made 30 saves for his first NHL victory.
At Washington, John Slaney scored with 13:29 left in regulation to lift the Los Angeles Kings to a 4-3 victory over the Capitals.
The Kings stormed back from a 3-0 first-period deficit by scoring four unanswered goals against Washington's Jim Carey. Slaney's third-period wrist shot snapped a 3-3 deadlock.
Kings goalie Stephane Fiset surrendered three goals in the first nine minutes, but stopped all 14 shots he faced over the final two periods.
In Phoenix, future Hall of Famer Mike Gartner had a goal and an assist and Darcy Wakaluk made 26 saves as the Coyotes beat the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim 4-2.
The third straight win for the former Winnipeg Jets ended the Ducks' three-game unbeaten streak.
Gartner, who turns 37 this month, scored with 2:35 left in the second period to break a 1-1 tie. Mike Stapleton extended the lead to 3-1 early in the third.
In Vancouver, Martin Gelinas had two goals and an assist and Mike Sillinger's goal with 4:35 left in the second period broke a 3-3 tie as the Canucks beat the St Louis Blues 5-3.
Trevor Linden assisted on both of Gelinas's goals and picked up his third by setting up Pavel Bure's insurance tally with 5:31 left.
In San Jose, the Boston Bruins erased a three-goal deficit by scoring five unanswered goals in a 5-3 win over the Sharks.
San Jose led 3-0 after Viktor Kozlov's goal at 3:25 of the second period.
Boston closed to within 3-2 after two periods and Ray Bourque set up two of Boston's three third-period goals as the Bruins outshot the Sharks 22-12 after the first period.
